checks: Equal total weights on the two endpoint fibers force exactly the Minkowski average at base zero. Both endpoints have area one and the middle dimensions are (1+R)/2 and (1+1/R)/2.

For tilt in [−1/2,1/2], the endpoint cap sum is affine and nonincreasing. Beyond the positive endpoint, the first cap has zero area and the second is nondecreasing; beyond the negative endpoint the first has area one.

Checked the rational threshold factorization, derivative and exact root-elimination formula. The comparison to (m_R+1)/3 follows by the strictly positive difference of squares with a positive unsquared left side.
Reflection and quasiconcavity give a middle-fiber maximum at the origin. A sufficiently large signed integer tilt isolates a containing ordinary halfplane of area at most one half at either endpoint.

At R=2, direct clipping gives areas 0, 9/16 and 3/4. The left supporting edge is nonempty and has zero planar measure. The constant section profiles retain unit mass, zero means and the exact midpoint rectangle.

overlap.comparison: That accepted equal-volume theorem is a mass-dependent lower bound at the actual mixed centroid. Its conclusion does not establish an axial upper bound or the independent absolute-credit obstruction proved here.

readability: The axial minimum concerns a single fixed continuous normal. It upper-bounds the full depth and does not identify the global all-direction minimum.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The reciprocal rectangles are actual compatible fibers and give the claimed all-tilt raw axial minimum and the upper bound at every feasible mark.
